bound_input_hash_summary.note: The compact binding list above intentionally preserves the 16/16 aggregate; the canonical request remains the authoritative per-file list.

obligations.text: All 16 bound inputs match their request hashes and the Build11 manifest, wheel, and native artifact digests match the fixed producer identity.
EvidenceLifecycle enforces PLANNED->RUNNING->SEALED->REVIEWED transitions, contiguous ordinals, previous-event links, and canonical event digests.
PLANNED binds an input digest and RUNNING/SEALED carry digests, but the config bytes/run label and the exact external producer identity are not closed by the reviewer.
The v2 replay path is the only active code path that appends REVIEWED and it binds the raw-manifest digest; the replay is independent of the producer module.
Event, state, ordinal, and prior-event edits fail without recomputing the chain, but a producer/run-label resign with a recomputed chain is accepted; artifact field sets are also not closed.
The v1 compatibility path remains readable without adding a lifecycle to the historical bundle.
The bound v2 runner and reviewer have no mutual import; the reviewer replays raw streams independently.
The bound T1-T4, aggregate-refinement, and native-round claim-boundary documents remain unchanged and are still explicitly conditional.
Critical and major counts are reported separately and this decision refuses PASS while major findings remain.

independent_reproduction.method: ephemeral Build11 formal-venv RCPSP raw run followed by a recomputed lifecycle and sidecar
independent_reproduction.observation: The manifest claimed the new run label and forged producer digests while the signed config artifact retained the old run label; reviewer verification still returned PASS.

findings.title: Bound producer identity is shape-checked, not identity-checked
findings.counterexample: _validate_producer_identity only requires BOUND_CLEAN_BUILD plus three 64-character strings (lines 189-205); it never compares source revision/tree, native_build_attestation, or the exact Build11 manifest digest. The independent reproduction supplied f/w/e/d digests and verify_raw_manifest returned PASS.
findings.impact: A raw bundle can be relabeled as a clean Build11 producer without being produced by revision 6d28923c or the recorded wheel/native artifacts, invalidating the Build11 evidence binding.

findings.title: Run-label and input-config identity are not closed
findings.counterexample: _validate_sealed_lifecycle checks lifecycle.run_label against manifest.run_label and the lifecycle digests against manifest fields, but never opens config.json to compare its run_label or recomputes input_config_sha256 from the bound config artifact. runner.py:42-73 hashes the caller's original bytes and writes a separately normalized config artifact. The reproduction changed only the manifest label and recomputed lifecycle events; verification passed while config.json retained the old label.
findings.impact: The manifest can be detached from the actual input configuration and assigned to a different run label while retaining a self-consistent lifecycle, breaking raw-to-run traceability.

findings.title: Self-resigned artifact/result fields are not schema-closed
findings.counterexample: verify_raw_manifest accepts artifact entries with arbitrary extra keys and checks only path/sha256/bytes (lines 64-88); read_signed_json/write_signed_json use a producer-rewritable SHA-256 sidecar (codec.py:51-55), and result.json has no exact field-set/schema validation before replay (reviewer.py:250-270). A producer can therefore resign the manifest/result and alter non-replayed identity metadata without an external anchor or rejection.
findings.impact: Exact artifact/result identity and provenance fields are mutable under a self-consistent resign, so an independent reviewer cannot distinguish the recorded Build11 bundle from a producer-rewritten bundle.
